messages:
micah: FYI customer reported a p99 token latency spike ~700ms for requests aimed at us-west this morning.
cheryl: any trace link?
micah: https://console.redwood.example/traces/trace-0xdeadbeef (redacted) — quick snippet: unexpected hop to eu-central.
micah: ```
trace: 0xdeadbeef
client -> ingest-us-west-02 (10.12.4.9)
ingest-us-west -> egress-us-west-01
egress-us-west-01 -> eu-peering-01 (35.156.210.7) [unexpected]
eu-peering-01 -> storage-us-west-01
latencies: hop3 +680ms
headers: x-region=us-west-2, x-eval-route=prefer-cost
```
dan: That eu-peering hop shouldn't happen for pinned routes. Could be new routing policy fallback. :thinking_face:
ops-bot: Deploy 2026-03-16T08:12 by infra/route-sync completed (routing-policy:v2)
cheryl: @dan @ops-bot did that deploy change interregion peering preferences?
dan: routing-policy:v2 added a soft-cost-fallback that prefers lower-cost egress when local pool is saturated. It should still honor x-pin-region though. Might be a bug.
micah: Repro steps I used:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "x-pin-region: us-west-2" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
micah: Normally ~120ms, but at 200qps from a single IP I reproduce egress to eu-peering and the ~700ms jump.
cheryl: paste full trace headers (x-egress-route, x-fallback-reason, x-routing-policy-version)?
micah: From trace headers:```
x-pin-region: us-west-2
x-egress-route: eu-peering-01
x-fallback-reason: pool_saturated_soft
x-routing-policy-version: v2
```
dan: "pool_saturated_soft" corresponds to the new soft fallback. Bug: we should not apply soft-cost-fallback to requests with x-pin-region. I'll open an infra ticket.
cheryl: Sending customer a short note: "We're investigating unexpected routing to EU egress under load; temporary workaround is to add x-force-local:true."
micah: Verified workaround: adding x-force-local:true keeps traffic in us-west even at 400qps in my tests.
support-sre: Filing incident P2 -> infra-routing. Attaching repro steps, trace links, perf logs. Ticket IR-2026-342.
ops-bot: Alert suppressed for duplicate trace groups.
dan: Plan: short-term revert the soft-cost-fallback part of routing-policy:v2 for pinned requests, push to canary.
cheryl: @micah please test canary once dan pushes; want confirmation before full rollback.
micah: will test — ETA ~10m.
(10m) micah: can confirm canary stops egress to eu-peering; p99 back to ~130ms. Updating customer.
cheryl: Follow-ups: 1) patch routing-policy to respect x-pin-region, 2) add unit/integration tests for soft-fallback gating, 3) enrich trace annotations with fallback reason and pool state. Will add to postmortem.
support-sre: Customer updated: "latency normalized, thank you" :white_check_mark:. Closing P2 after confirmation; ticket remains until fix merged.
